name: Rivera Family
persona: Marisol (38) and Daniel (41) Rivera live in Oak Cliff, Dallas with their kids Sofia (15) and Mateo (9) and Marisol's mother Elena (68). Marisol owns Rivera's Panadería, a neighbourhood bakery with about $1.3M of revenue in 2025; her owner draws arrive in lumps that follow catering orders and the holiday season. Daniel has steady W-2 pay as a logistics supervisor. Financially solid (good credit, home equity, healthy savings) but cash is lumpy, and money lives in six places. Their home is worth about $410k. They are weighing a second bakery location (about $250k build-out, maybe an SBA loan), Elena's rising medical costs and a college fund. Hero demo household: no planted fraud, one benign medical-bill outlier.

name: Okafor Household
persona: Amara (28, nurse) and Chidi (29, QA engineer) Okafor rent in Lakewood, Dallas. Student loans, a car loan and high credit-card utilization hold their scores down while they save a House Fund for a first home in about two years. A September account takeover drained $4,650 from the House Fund and a card-testing burst hit their cash-back card in August.

name: Nguyen Household
persona: Tom (72) and Linh (70) Nguyen are retired in Garland. Pension plus Social Security, a CD ladder, two IRAs and a paid-off house worth about $285k. On Oct 21 a caller posing as their grandson Kevin ('in jail, don't tell Mom and Dad') talked them into buying $2,000 of gift cards across four stores in two hours: the demo elder-scam case.

name: Patel Household
persona: Priya Patel (34) is a single parent in Arlington with an 8-year-old son, Aarav. Part-time dental-office payroll plus DoorDash, Instacart and Uber Eats earnings that swing week to week. Thin cushion, overdraft fees and a high-APR installment loan. Her credit union export is messy: duplicates, garbled merchant names, an impossible $9,999,999.99 coffee and postings dated in the future.

name: Brooks Family
persona: Terrence (46, operations manager) and Danielle (44, assistant principal) Brooks live in DeSoto with their 16-year-old Jordan and Terrence's father Walter (74), who receives Social Security and helps with bills but needs a part-time home aide. A 3.4% mortgage, an SUV loan and a 529 plan for Jordan that is behind target. Home worth about $330k. Steady incomes, tight sandwich-generation budget; clean books apart from a benign roof-repair outlier and one double-posted pharmacy charge.
